ai.description: *Limnonectes mawlyndipi* is a small frog (SVL ~35–40 mm). It features a brown dorsum with darker markings, a pale mid-dorsal stripe, and a distinct dark triangular patch between the eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Limnonectes mawlyndipi* is best distinguished by its distinct, prominent glandular folds on the flanks, which are absent or significantly less developed in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Mawlindip frog inhabits moist, evergreen subtropical forests in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, typically found near rocky streams at elevations around 1,200–1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Mawlyndip frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky, humid stream banks of its native habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Limnonectes mawlyndipi* breeds during the monsoon season, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in terrestrial nests near water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Limnonectes mawlyndipi* is endemic to the East Khasi Hills in Meghalaya, India, where it inhabits high-altitude streams at elevations around 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Mawlyndip Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "tink" notes. These calls are typically heard from rocky, fast-flowing streams in forested hill habitats.
